marble.name: Scale of the Solar System
marble.subject: Science
marble.description: Use scale models, diagrams, or calculations to represent the relative sizes and distances of objects in the solar system, understanding that the distances between planets are enormously larger than the planets themselves
marble.prompt: Has you ever built or looked at a scale model of the solar system? Can they explain why the planets would need to be spread across a whole playing field to be the right distance apart?

cluster.summary: Your child is beginning their journey into space science — learning about astronauts and the Moon's phases, identifying objects in the sky, and discovering that we live in a solar system with other planets.

misconceptions: Thinking the planets are close together and the solar system is crowded (from textbook diagrams), rather than mostly vast empty space.
Assuming a single scale model can show both true planet sizes and true distances easily — missing that a same-scale model needs an enormous area.
Reading the common 'planets in a neat row, evenly spaced' picture as accurate for size and distance.
Confusing scaling SIZE with scaling DISTANCE — shrinking planets and gaps by different unstated amounts and not noticing.
Believing the outer planets are only a little farther than the inner ones, underestimating how distances balloon toward Neptune.
representations: Beach-ball Sun / pea Earth ~26 m away — the anchor scale comparison
Two separate models: a SIZE model (planets shrunk in proportion) and a DISTANCE model (spacing shrunk in proportion), shown to be incompatible on one scale
A scale ratio / proportion tool: Scale size ÷ real size = Scale distance ÷ real distance
A 'toilet-paper' / bead-on-a-string distance model pacing planets out along a line
A to-scale strip the child must scroll a long way across to travel from the Sun to the outer planets
authoredAnswer: A correct performance applies one consistent scale: with the Sun as a ~30 cm beach ball, the Earth-pea is placed about 25–30 metres away, and Neptune ends up roughly 30 times farther still — hundreds of metres away, likely off the end of the playground. wrongAnswers.revealedBy: child clusters the planets a few steps from the Sun, hugely under-scaling the distances to match familiar diagrams
wrongAnswers.fix: Physically pace out the true scaled distances so the vast empty gaps are FELT; contrast with the compressed textbook image and name it as not-to-scale.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: child scales the ball and pea correctly but squashes the distances (or stretches distances while over-sizing the planets)
wrongAnswers.fix: Scaffold, don't reteach: remind them a scale model must use ONE ruler for both — measure sizes and distances with the same scale factor and check they match.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: child sets the planets edge-to-edge or with gaps similar to the planets' own sizes
wrongAnswers.fix: Show the real gaps are thousands of times the planet sizes — the solar system is overwhelmingly empty space.
